'''Satwant Pasricha''' was the head of Department of Clinical Psychology at [[NIMHANS]], National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences at [[Bangalore]].<ref>K. Sekar, et al., [http://stg1.kar.nic.in/nimhans/dis_man/man_tsu1.pdf Tsunami: Psychosocial care for individuals & families]{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, January 2005, p. 7. Accessed 2009-01-27.</ref> She also worked for a time at the [[University of Virginia School of Medicine]] in the USA.<ref>David Barker and Satwant Pasricha. [http://jas.sagepub.com/cgi/pdf_extract/14/3-4/231 Reincarnation Cases in Fatehabad: A Systematic Survey of North India] ''[[Journal of Asian and African Studies]]'', Vol. 14, No. 3-4, 1979, p. 231.</ref> Pasricha investigates [[reincarnation]]<ref>[http://www.rediff.com/news/1998/jul/30rebir.htm NIMHANS doctor attempts to prove life after death], ''Rediff on the NeT'', July 30, 1998. Accessed 2009-01-27.</ref> and [[near-death experience]]s.<ref name=riti>M D Riti, [http://www.rediff.com/news/1999/apr/06pas.htm To Hell, and Back], ''Rediff on the NeT'', April 6, 1999. Accessed 2009-01-27.</ref> Pasricha co-authored the 2011 book ''Making sense of near-death experiences'', which was Highly Commended in the Psychiatry category at the 2012 [[British Medical Association]] Book Awards.<ref>{{cite book |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=Qsc3PPps5O8C&q=satwant+pasricha&pg=PA7  |title=Making sense of near-death experiences: A handbook for clinicians |author1=S Pasricha |author2=DJ Wilde |author3=M Perera |author4=K Jagadheesan |date=2011 |publisher=Jessica Kingsley Publishers |isbn=9780857003423 }}</ref>

==Work==
Pasricha has investigated and participated in about 500 cases of reincarnation involving children (referred to as subjects) since 1973 who claim to remember previous lives. She became interested in working in [[parapsychology]] because she was not satisfied with the conventional explanations of certain paranormal or unusual behavior.<ref name=bio>[http://www.pflyceum.org/49.html Satwant Pasricha], ''The Biographical Dictionary of Parapsychology''. Accessed 2009-01-27.</ref>

Pasricha studies not just the characteristics of reincarnation prevalent in India, but also suggests ways they are similar or different from those of people in other countries.<ref name=riti/> She collaborated with [[Ian Stevenson]] in reincarnation research beginning in the 1970s.<ref>Ian Stevenson, ''[[Where Reincarnation and Biology Intersect]]'', Greenwood Publishing Group, 1997, p. 59. {{ISBN|0-275-95189-8}}.</ref>

She joined NIMHANS ([[Deemed University]]) as a faculty in December 1980 as a lecturer in Clinical Parapsychology; and then was promoted to assistant professor, associate professor and additional professor of clinical psychology. She is also involved in clinical work such as patient care and teaching and research in the areas of her interest at NIMHANS.<ref name=bio/>

Satwant Pasricha of the [[Maulana Azad Medical College]] appreciates her work on the subject, but he also places not-verifiable truth like "rebirth" and “reincarnation” out of the domain of the scientific knowledge. Many other scientists label them as a hallucinatory experience and as "a physiological state occurring within an oxygen starved brain."<ref>{{cite journal| author=R. C. Jiloha|title=Relevance of parapsychology in psychiatric practice: Response to Dr. R. C. Jiloha's comments|journal=Indian J Psychiatry|date= April 1, 2014|volume= 56 |issue=2 |page= 208|pmc=4040079|doi=10.4103/0019-5545.130517|pmid=24891719 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
